_note: Kid explanations (<= 20 words, spoken-ready) for words the crew and our own lines use. 'forms' are spellings to match. 'source': a NASA page for a term no crew clip says (vocab.py prefers the crew recording). 'crew_jargon': false keeps an everyday word (rover, ice) from pausing crew audio to explain it (moments.py).

albedo.explain: How bright or dark a surface is in sunlight.

ejecta.explain: Rock and dust thrown out when something smashes into the Moon.

limb.explain: The edge of the Moon as we see it.

terminator.explain: The line between the Moon's day side and night side.

mare.explain: A dark, flat 'sea' of old cooled lava.

rays.explain: Bright streaks of splashed rock spreading out from a crater.

basin.explain: A giant crater, hundreds of kilometers wide.

plateau.explain: A big raised area of land with a flat top.

relief.explain: How bumpy the ground is: hills, holes and ridges.

hummocky.explain: Covered in lots of small, rounded bumps.

swirl.explain: A bright, curly pattern painted on the Moon's surface.

impact flash.explain: A tiny burst of light when a space rock hits.

corona.explain: The Sun's glowing outer air, seen when the Sun is hidden.

earthset.explain: Earth sinking out of sight behind the Moon's edge.

earthrise.explain: Earth coming up over the Moon's edge.

crater.explain: A round hole made when a space rock crashed in.

central peak.explain: A mountain in a crater's middle that bounced up.

pyroclastic.explain: Made by volcanoes spraying out tiny glass beads.

lava.explain: Melted rock that flowed out, then cooled hard.

highlands.explain: The bright, old, bumpy parts of the Moon.

pillowing.explain: Soft, puffy-looking rounded shapes, like pillows.

blanketing.explain: A layer of thrown-out rock covering the ground.

orbit.explain: Going around and around something in space.

far side.explain: The Moon's side that always faces away from Earth.

near side.explain: The Moon's side that always faces Earth: the face we see every night.

rille.explain: A long, winding groove on the Moon, often cut by flowing lava.

source.title: NASA Science: what the Moon is made of

impact.explain: A space rock smashing into the Moon. Every crater is an old impact.

phase.explain: How much of the Moon's sunny side we can see from Earth.

eclipse.explain: When the Sun, Earth and Moon line up and one blocks the other's light.

solar storm.explain: A burst of fast particles from the Sun. Astronauts take shelter until it passes.

millisievert.explain: A unit for how much space radiation your body gets. Smaller numbers are safer.

shelter.explain: A safe room with thick walls that blocks space radiation during a solar storm.

rover.explain: A car or a robot that drives across the Moon's surface.

permanently shadowed region.explain: A deep crater floor the Sun never reaches. It is so cold that ice stays frozen.

source.title: NASA Science: water and ice on the Moon

ice.explain: Frozen water. Moon ice could give astronauts water, air and rocket fuel.

source.title: NASA Science: water and ice on the Moon
